prompt:
Create one finished flat opaque 16:9 landscape SNS poster promoting a weekend houseplant market. Use case: ads-marketing. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Build a painterly editorial sequence about choosing living plants and enjoying their daily care. Three unequal rectilinear painted views and their shared edges organize the whole poster: a tall close view at the left of overlapping philodendron and rubber-plant leaves beside a honey-lit window; a much wider shallow view across the upper middle/right of varied terracotta and glazed pots on a plant-market table, showing small plants alongside a mature branching tree, with a hand lightly comparing one pot to its neighbours; a tight square at the middle right showing a well-rooted leafy plant being settled into a real clay pot, one hand supporting the root ball and the other steadying the rim. Distinct leaves attach convincingly to stems, pots have open rims, thickness, bases and contact shadows, and the hands have clear ownership and contact. Fill the views with substantive botanical masses, pottery and directional light. They evoke related experiences rather than an invented numbered tutorial. No labels on pots or incidental letters.

Use expressive opaque gouache and oil-like brush-built masses, controlled bristle edges, deep indigo and plum shadows, luminous varied leaf greens, and selective honey window light. No photographic rendering, toy forms or tape motif. Preserve the rectilinear intervals and contrasting distances; the left close view is tall, the market view panoramic, the care view square. The painted sequence must carry the composition, not decorate a conventional headline/information board.

The central caption hinge sits directly below the panoramic market view and beside the square care view. Its invitation is the main typographic entry, a warm ivory medium-weight Korean serif with clear open counters, restrained stroke contrast and a noticeably stronger body than the prose. Set it in two natural phrase lines. Beneath it, the explanation starts immediately on the same stable left edge, in four calm full reading lines using the supplied line groups. Give this entire paragraph a broad uninterrupted reading area and substantial mature Korean sans letter bodies, square syllable rhythm, consistent moderate stems, generous counters and normal meaningful word spaces. Plan for comfortable reading at a 720-pixel-wide SNS view: about 15–17-pixel body appearance is a design starting point, not an output-size instruction. Keep typography crisply planar with no brush texture, perspective or artificial distress on letters. Rebalance image crops and the quiet identity area if needed to make the actual explanation and all visit details fit at a readable size.

From the final prose line, one short downward continuation on this same caption axis leads into the market name, slightly stronger than the paragraph but weaker than the invitation. Date and hours follow together as a nearby local row; the venue follows closely. Pair access and care offer below, with URL immediately after. Use clear lining numerals and extended midline en dashes whose length remains distinct from a short hyphen; maintain colons, periods, middle dots, ampersand and URL spelling. The full useful visit group belongs to the central continuation, not remote corners or a tiny footer.

At the lower edge of the tall left painted view place the quieter Korean identity in two modest word lines, its Latin companion directly beside it with balanced optical weight. Join the slogan to that identity as a supportive sentence, with sensible phrase wrapping if needed. This left identity stays appreciably quieter than the central invitation. Give all printed copy clean high contrast against the dark ground. Image boundaries, not boxes around every text group, create the reading rhythm.

Print exactly the following twelve entries, once each. The line breaks below are soft design wrapping; retain every glyph, word boundary and punctuation. Do not print this instruction, entry labels, numbers or quotation marks. These are the only letters/numbers allowed anywhere in the poster:

One independent complete poster, not multiple poster designs, a comparison sheet, contact sheet, framed print or room mockup. The three painted views are legitimate scenes within this one coherent finished poster. No new copy, logo, watermark, QR or decorative pseudo-writing. Exclude passive solid/near-solid/split-field gothic headline/date/information templates with subordinate images, tiny-image or texture/font substitutions and empty-room text-board dressing. Keep the positive image-led editorial sequence, intimate plant care, central invitation → explanation → visit reading route and quieter left identity.
